description: We are Team Skyora from Dhaka, Bangladesh. We are participating in the "Create Health Monitoring Software for Astronauts on Space Missions" challenge. Our goal is to build software to track astronaut vital signs and health metrics using data visualization and tracking systems.
summary: AstroMind is a research prototype for monitoring astronaut health during deep-space missions, where communication delays can make timely medical support difficult. It brings simulated crew-health trends and habitat hazards into one dashboard. Personal baselines across five health domains help surface changes, while explainable alerts show the contributing signals and context. A separate mission simulator supports scenario presets, sensor overrides, and ocular and reflex self-checks. AstroMind links crew-reviewed alerts to care, monitoring, and recovery workflows to support mission-aware decisions. All telemetry and scenarios shown are simulated. The prototype is not a diagnostic tool, medical device, or substitute for qualified medical care. Created by Team Skyora for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge; not endorsed by NASA.
details:
ASTROMIND — DEEP-SPACE CREW HEALTH PROTOTYPE

THE CHALLENGE
During deep-space missions, communication delays can slow access to medical support. Crew-health trends and shared habitat hazards need to be considered together.

THE PROJECT
AstroMind is an offline-first browser prototype for exploring this challenge. Its desktop mission console brings simulated crew telemetry, personal baselines, mission conditions, and self-check results into one interface. A separate /simulator page lets users select profiles, try preset scenarios, adjust demonstration sensors, and explore ocular and reflex checks.

HOW IT WORKS
Five deterministic health-domain checks and crew–habitat hazard correlation work alongside local, explainable statistical models. AstroMind surfaces contributing signals and presents illustrative GREEN/AMBER/RED triage, EVA-readiness status, and a crew-reviewed care and recovery workflow. A one-way safety gate prevents the ML layer from lowering deterministic AMBER or RED alerts.

TECHNOLOGY & SAFETY
Built with Python, FastAPI, WebSockets, and browser-based HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. It runs with local fixtures and requires no GPU or hosted LLM. All telemetry and scenarios are simulated. AstroMind is a research prototype—not a medical device, diagnostic tool, or NASA-endorsed system. Developed by Team Skyora for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge.
